How Portolan works, end to end

Portolan reads the places your customer knowledge already sits, writes down each fact with the exact spot it came from, and keeps the result current. The diagram below has two views. Press Play and it walks the whole path, one step at a time.

9 stages

    Stage 1 of 9 · Sources

    The knowledge already exists, scattered across recorded calls, the CRM and the emails it logs, support tickets, documents, and public news feeds.

    One edge, said out loud. In the first version, everyone signed in at your organization sees everything in the graph: per-person permissions are not built yet. When two notes flatly disagree, Portolan keeps both with their dates; if the dates settle which is newer, the older one is marked replaced automatically, and when they do not, the pair goes into the review queue for a person to sort out.

    The names, dates and quote above come from Portolan’s synthetic test corpus (corpus/truth-table.yaml, 2026-09-12). Halvard Medical, Ashgrove and the Tidewater T2 are invented, so the test can be scored against a known answer. Everything drawn on this page is from portolan-spec-v2.md, provenance-chain.md and surfacing-and-weekly-report.md, all dated 2026-09-12.

    From knowing to doing

    Each week, before the report goes out, the system looks for candidates worth a closer look: a theme that is new or rising, an account with a renewal coming up and a history that has gone quiet or turned to complaints, a commitment that is past its date, a standing question still open, or a pricing or competitor mention at a large account.

    For each candidate, a dedicated researcher reads the graph the same way a person would, through the same tools: search, open a note, open a source, ask for a count. It may only hand back a card whose evidence is copied word for word from stored claims, whose numbers come only from counts the system itself computed, and whose one or two sentences of reasoning are checked by a second model against that evidence. Anything that does not clear that bar is dropped, and the drop is logged, not hidden.

    The cards that survive land in the review queue as proposals, not actions. A person reads each one and confirms it, and only then does an action exist: it gets an owner (the account’s own owner, unless the evidence names someone else), a due date, and a link back to the sentence it came from. Confirmed actions show up on the Actions page, grouped by owner, and in that week’s report.

    Example a confirmed action, from the synthetic corpus

    “Follow up with Renee Castillo at Anchor Bay Surgical Partners on the small-volume discount request for Tidewater T2 consumables.”

    owner: Sam Okafor · due: 2026-09-27
    evidence: “Renee Castillo from Anchor Bay Surgical Partners asked about a small-volume discount on Tidewater T2 consumables” — S-ticket-043
    finding: no response or commitment recorded for the account after that request

    A person confirmed this card in the review queue; that is what turned it into an action.

    The names, dates and evidence above come from Portolan’s synthetic test corpus (corpus/truth-table.yaml, 2026-09-12) and its ticket export, S-ticket-043. Anchor Bay Surgical Partners, Renee Castillo and Sam Okafor are invented, the same way Ashgrove is above. The Act stage itself is specified in actions-and-owners-2026-09-19.md, dated 2026-09-19.

    Transcript
    [intro]

    Here is how Portolan works, from the first phone call to the sentence a reader sees on screen. The diagram has two views. The first shows what happens to a piece of knowledge. The second shows where it lives. Let's start with the first.

    [how-1]

    Everything begins with sources. Your customer knowledge already exists. It is in recorded calls, in the CRM and the emails it logs, in support tickets, in shared documents, and in public feeds like a customer's company page. Portolan does not ask anyone to write anything new. It reads what is already there.

    [how-2]

    Intake stores the original exactly as it arrived, strips the junk and the quoted text that piles up in email threads, and marks every line so it can be found again later. Nothing is summarized yet.

    [how-3]

    The filter keeps what touches customers and sets the rest aside. It routes on things the CRM already knows, like a contact's email address, rather than guessing from names. And a small sample of what was set aside is checked every day, so if the filter starts missing things, the weekly report says so.

    [how-4]

    Extraction is where a model reads each source once. A small, inexpensive model. It writes down the facts it finds, one fact per line, and for each one it records the exact spot in the original: the timestamp in the call, the message in the thread, the page in the document. A fact with no spot is thrown out.

    [how-5]

    The registry matches every name to the customer list from the CRM. Mercy is not a guess; it is a record number. When a name could mean two things, Portolan does not choose. It attaches the fact to the parent they share, or asks a person.

    [how-6]

    Merge decides what each fact is. New, a repeat of something already known, a detail that extends it, or a contradiction. When two facts disagree, both are kept with their dates. The old one is marked as replaced, not deleted. So the graph can always answer what was believed on any given day.

    [how-7]

    The result is the graph: small linked notes. One for each account, each person, each product, each kind of signal, each theme, each decision, each action, and each source. Every sentence in a note points back to where it came from.

    [how-8]

    Keeping it honest is scheduled work. Every night the crawl reads only what changed. A checker walks the graph for broken links, stale notes, and missing sources. A rewrite pass tidies notes that have grown messy, and a second reader re-checks a sample of sources with a stronger model to count what the first pass missed.

    [how-9]

    Then the ways in. A chat, where every sentence carries its source. A viewer, where you can walk from an answer to a note, to the source note, to the original recording at the exact minute. A weekly report that assembles itself from what changed. And a door for your own AI tools, so they can ask the graph questions too.

    [where-intro]

    Now the second view: where the data lives.

    [where-1]

    On the left are your systems. Your call recorder, your CRM with the emails it logs, your ticket desk, your documents, and the public feeds you choose. Portolan reads from them. It never holds a mailbox password.

    [where-2]

    Each source is copied in once and kept as the original. That copy is the thing every citation eventually opens.

    [where-3]

    A queue hands work to the pipeline in order, so nothing is lost when a step fails. A failed source is retried, and if it keeps failing it is listed, not forgotten.

    [where-4]

    The models that read text run inside Amazon's cloud, under the healthcare agreement that covers the whole path. Text goes in, facts come back. Nothing is used to train anything.

    [where-5]

    The database holds the notes, the facts, the search index, and the customer list. One database per customer. Yours is not mixed with anyone else's.

    [where-6]

    The web app is what people use: the chat, the viewer, the reports, and the place to fix a note by hand when a machine got it wrong. Every fix is signed with a name and a date.

    [where-7]

    When a reader follows a citation all the way back, the original opens through a private link that expires. Every open is logged.

    [where-8]

    The door for your own AI tools reads from the graph and never writes to it.

    [where-9]

    All of this sits in your own locked room inside our building. Nothing leaves that room except what you ask for.

    [chain]

    One more thing, because it is the point of the whole system. Every answer shows its work. The sentence you read links to a note. The note links to the source note, which says who was on the call and when. The source note opens the original at the exact spot. If any link in that chain is missing, the sentence is not shown.

    [outro]

    Two edges, said out loud. In this first version, everyone who signs in at your organization sees everything. And when two notes disagree, Portolan keeps both with their dates but does not yet flag the pair for you. That is a later build. Everything else you just heard is running today.

    [correction]

    Correction, 2026-09-20: disagreeing notes are now flagged for review; the permissions edge still stands.

    Working name. Design as of 2026-09-20. Every crawl reads from one Company context note that says who the tenant is, what they sell, and what counts as a signal.
